newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes expanding family leave act.
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes expanding family leave act.

text.p: Keeping a campaign promise, President Clinton proposed on Saturday to let workers take time off to take their children or elderly relatives to the doctor or attend parent-teacher meetings.

In his weekly radio address, Clinton proposed an expansion of the Family and Medical Leave Act, four years after he signed the law allowing employees to take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave to care for family emergencies.
"Now we must make it even easier for parents to live up to their responsibilities to their children and to their employers. Today I call upon Congress to expand the family leave law," he said.

He said he wanted to expand the law to give parents an additional 24 hours of unpaid leave each year to take a child or a elderly relative to a regular doctors' appointment or to attend parent-teacher conferences at school.
"In so doing we will make our families stronger and our workers more productive, building the kind of country and economy we all want for our children," he said.

Clinton said he also wanted to address the fact that still too many people did not know about the family leave law. He said the government was launching a multimedia public education campaign to spread the word about it because 40 percent of workers covered by it have never heard of it.
The centerpiece of the new campaign is a new toll-free hotline that Americans can call to learn about family leave. It is 1-800-959-FMLA.

Clinton had proposed during his 1996 re-election campaign that the family leave law be expanded. At the time then-Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole had opposed the plan because it would increase the burden on employers.
